summary: Rerank endpoint returns low-similarity after customer-side embedding serialization (endianness) — CPU fallback and latency spike
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that reranking results show unexpectedly low similarity scores after upgrading their client integration. Impact: Production rerank calls for BrightSearch search pipeline are returning highly divergent orderings; search latency spikes from baseline ~120ms p50 to 800-1200ms, and some requests fall back to a CPU-based compatibility path causing 503s. Environment: Production API (us-east-1), embed-large-v2 model. Initial hypothesis: mismatched binary embedding serialization (endianness or float32 vs float16 byte layout) on the client side causes the server to detect incompatible vector signatures and trigger a slow code path which includes extra validation and CPU normalization.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer uses custom client to serialize embeddings as raw little-endian floats into a binary protobuf payload and POSTs to /v1/embeddings
2) Server accepts embedding payload but logs a "signature-mismatch" for vector checksum at ingestion stage (no immediate 4xx)

3) Rerank call with those embeddings hits serving-runtime compatibility check, triggers CPU fallback normalization, then executes similarity computation on a fallback path leading to increased latency and sometimes 503s under load
4) Replacing client serialization with Redwood official SDK (which sends base64-encoded big-endian float32 array) produces expected rerank ordering and restored latency

investigation_notes: Support reproduced locally by serializing float32 in little-endian vs SDK big-endian: big-endian base64 payload reproduces expected scores; little-endian raw binary triggers checksum warning and CPU path
Checksum routine expects network byte order (big-endian) for historical reasons; permissive parser exists for backward compatibility but incurs slower path and extra normalization steps
Observed that legacy permissive-parser also performs element-wise NaN/Inf checks and converts to host float format on CPU which is expensive under high QPS
No model weight or inference graph changes on back-end; this appears purely input-serialization compatibility issue
Potential for customers to silently degrade quality if they use custom serialization without matching Redwood's expected layout
comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 - Support (Aisha Patel): Hi BrightSearch team — thanks for the report. Can you confirm which client library and serialization method you're using to send embeddings? Also please include a sample base64 payload if possible.

2026-03-10 15:40 - Customer (BrightSearch / Dev): We're using an in-house C++ pipeline that writes raw float32 little-endian into the protobuf bytes field for performance. We switched from the official SDK last week after a custom perf optimization.

2026-03-10 16:10 - Support (Aisha Patel): Thanks — we're seeing evidence of a byte-order mismatch on our side. We're escalating to Eng (Marco) to confirm and propose mitigation. We'll aim to provide a temporary workaround within 24h.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Eng (Marco Reyes): Confirmed: server expects big-endian (network order) encoded float32 arrays by default. The permissive fallback is enabled but routes to CPU normalization and heavy validation. Recommending immediate customer workaround: use Redwood SDK or send base64(big-endian) floats. Investigating long-term: add explicit detection and an optimized fast-path for little-endian clients to avoid CPU fallback.

2026-03-12 11:55 - Customer (BrightSearch / Dev): Applied SDK-based serialization; rerank ordering restored and latency returned to baseline. Thanks for triage. Please advise on long-term roadmap as we may keep custom pipeline for other reasons.
resolution: Workaround provided: revert to Redwood official SDK serialization or explicitly encode float32 arrays as big-endian/base64 when sending embeddings. Customer confirmed recovery after applying workaround.

Short-term engineering fix: disable permissive fallback for malformed headers in high-QPS customer routes (will force 4xx instead of CPU fallback) — gated behind support opt-in. Patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345

Long-term action items: (1) implement a lightweight endian-detection fast-path that can convert little-endian payloads on the GPU path without full CPU normalization; (2) update public SDK docs and add a conformance test that detects incorrect byte-order during onboarding; (3) create a support runbook to triage serialization mismatches.
Follow-up tasks created: INT-5718 (implement endian fast-path), DOC-284 (sdk serialization conformance guide)
Status: Partial fix — customer restored. Engineering tasks scheduled under internal backlog.
